summary: Lunar Lens is an API for comparing sunlight and direct Earth visibility across lunar landing sites. Given a location and time range, it uses NASA lunar elevation data and NASA/JPL Sun and Earth positions to calculate when terrain blocks either body. The public web app demonstrates the API with an interactive 3D surface view and visibility timeline. We built the API for programmatic analysis, so researchers and mission planners can compare candidate sites and use the results in their own tools.
details:
Purpose

Lunar Lens was built for the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge. Near the lunar south pole, the Sun and Earth can sit low on the horizon, where local terrain can block sunlight or a direct view of Earth. The Lunar Lens API lets researchers and mission planners evaluate those conditions across candidate sites and time ranges.

API and data

The API returns terrain profiles and Sun and Earth visibility timelines in JSON or CSV. It calculates the terrain skyline from NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter elevation grids, searching up to 480 km from the selected site by default. It compares that skyline with apparent Sun and Earth positions from NASA/JPL Horizons. Structured results let users script comparisons across candidate sites, import the output into their own analysis tools, and combine visibility with other site selection criteria.

Public demo

The public web app demonstrates what the API returns. Visitors can select a site on the Moon, choose a UTC time range, and explore the results through a 3D surface view and a color-coded timeline. The API uses Hono on Cloudflare Workers, and the demo uses React, TypeScript, and Three.js.

How to interpret the results

Visibility is based on the center of each body relative to the calculated skyline. The public demo uses hourly samples, so its timeline transitions have hourly resolution. The results describe geometric visibility and can inform further analysis of solar power or communications.

AI assistance

Our team used AI tools for research, assistance with parts of the code and troubleshooting, and writing and editing. OpenAI Codex assisted with repository review and documentation.
dataRefs: NASA Moon Trek / LROC WAC mosaic (surface imagery)
NASA PDS LOLA LDEM_64 and LDEM_16 V3.1 (elevation grids)
NASA SVS CGI Moon Kit (globe textures)
NASA SLDEM2015 (regional reference and geometry tests)
NASA PDS LOLA polar grids (retained data and loader tests)
projectRefs: Astronomy Engine (globe orientation, lighting, and apparent body sizes)
